why: The good film with one analogy added to its reveal: the gas tail streams behind the comet like smoke behind a train, along the path it has flown. The analogy maps the tail onto the comet's path, so the viewer learns the misconception the film breaks (the tail as a wake); the devices row grades a device that maps a part onto the wrong thing Poor. Its maps and breaks_at are filled, so no pre-check sees it: only a reader does.
judging_10: judging 10 asks the calibration run for reject on every seeded case. devices is a house-strength row, and a Poor on a house-strength criterion yields consider, never reject; it is not one of the four criteria that decide a film. review.logline: A comet's tail leads it away from the Sun because sunlight and a wind from the Sun push it, not because it trails behind.
review.synopsis: A comet leaves the Sun tail first; sunlight is too weak to explain the gas tail; Biermann proposes a wind from the Sun, and the film likens the gas tail to smoke trailing a train along its path; Mariner 2 measures the wind; the opening comet is seen again.

flags.problem: The analogy maps the gas tail onto the path the comet has flown, as smoke trails a train, so the viewer learns the tail is a wake: the belief the film set out to break. The tail points along the wind, away from the Sun.
flags.fix: Map the tail onto the wind, not the path: a windsock points where the wind goes, not where its pole moves; then say where it breaks: unlike a windsock, a comet has two tails.
flags.quote: the gas tail streams behind the comet like smoke behind a train, along the path it has flown.

first_minute.promise_match: The comet and its tail are on screen and named at once.
first_minute.question_and_stakes: Why the tail leads; the same wind reached Quebec in 1989.
first_minute.gap: why a comet leaving the Sun has its tail in front

problems.problem: The analogy maps the gas tail onto the comet's path (smoke behind a train), which teaches the wake the film breaks.
problems.fix: Map the tail onto the wind instead (a windsock), and say where it breaks: a comet has two tails.
